remarks.name: Thariq
remarks.role: Claude Code anthropicai. prev YC W20, spc, medialab
remarks.text:
If you showed me Claude Code today in 2018, I would have thought it was AGI.

We have already absorbed a dramatic amount of change in the profession of software engineering and society as a whole. But still, we’re starting to see cracks.

Things are accelerating faster than I can honestly stay on top of. Most people I know in AI are tired but powering through. I fear we will need more than that.

We need time to harden our systems, and for society to deliberate in how this technology is used and deployed.

I have a fairly low p(doom), I am confident that we can get through this! Humanity is incredibly reslient and adaptable, but this comes from our ability to make hard decisions- like this one, together.
remarks.translation: 如果我在2018年看到今天的Claude Code，我会以为那就是AGI。我们已经吸收了软件工程行业乃至整个社会发生的巨量变化。但即便如此，我们开始看到裂痕。事情加速得比我能够真正跟上的速度还快。我认识的大多数AI领域的人都很疲惫，但仍在咬牙坚持。我担心我们需要的远不止这些。我们需要时间来加固我们的系统，也需要社会有时间来审慎思考这项技术该如何使用和部署。我对末日概率的估计相当低，我有信心我们能挺过去！人类极其坚韧、适应力极强，但这源于我们做出艰难决定的能力——就像这个决定一样，一起做出。

remarks.name: Alex Albert
remarks.role: Research AnthropicAI. Opinions are my own!
remarks.text:
Worth spending a few minutes this weekend to read this essay in full. 

Embedded evaluators might sound unusual in tech but it's pretty normal in other industries. Big banks have federal examiners with desks in the building and every nuclear plant in the US has inspectors who work on site full time. I think frontier AI labs should work the same way and this is a very practical first step.
remarks.translation: 值得这个周末花几分钟完整读一读这篇文章。嵌入式评估员在科技行业听起来可能不太寻常，但在其他行业却相当普遍。大型银行里有联邦检查员在楼内设办公桌，美国每一座核电站都有全职驻场的检查员。我认为前沿AI实验室也应该采用同样的方式，而这是一个非常切实可行的第一步。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
Before we solve AI alignment, we have a pretty serious human alignment problem. 

It is jarring to see the bad-faith reaction to Dario's piece from so many sides. I don't agree with every point of his essay but do believe it is a thoughtful piece everyone should read. It builds on some of the ideas @demishassabis  raised in July.

It is clear we need to focus on aligning amongst us humans on a few questions:

What is the opportunity, risks, second-order effects?

How do we measure all of this?

How do companies, governments and countries coordinate?

AI will benefit humanity if we can get our act together and move together.
remarks.translation: 在我们解决AI对齐问题之前，我们面临着一个相当严重的人类对齐问题。看到各方对达里奥文章如此恶意的反应，实在令人震惊。我并不完全同意他文章中的每一个观点，但我确实认为这是一篇深思熟虑的文章，每个人都应该读一读。它建立在@demishassabis七月提出的一些想法之上。很明显，我们需要专注于在人类之间就几个问题达成一致：机会、风险、二阶效应是什么？我们如何衡量这一切？公司、政府和国家之间如何协调？如果我们能齐心协力、共同行动，AI将造福人类。

remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
https://t.co/OL0LzGsXKY can now orchestrate subagents with different models & reasoning efforts.

e.g: Fable planning and Grok executing. Fable is a genius, Grok is a fast workhorse.

① Simple. 𝙰𝙶𝙴𝙽𝚃𝚂.𝚖𝚍 or your prompt can indicate this preference.

② Steer as you please. It’s extremely enjoyable to use. You just talk to the agent and interrupt at will.

Worth noting this works with any model, any gateway. No fancy server-side routing. Just harnessing (no pun intended) the model’s intelligence and ability to orchestrate.
remarks.translation: https://t.co/OL0LzGsXKY 现在可以编排具有不同模型和推理努力程度的子代理。例如：Fable 负责规划，Grok 负责执行。Fable 是个天才，Grok 是快速的工作马。① 简单。𝙰𝙶𝙴𝙽𝚃𝚂.𝚖𝚍 或你的提示词可以表明这一偏好。② 随心操控。用起来极其愉快。你只需与代理对话，并可随意打断。值得注意的是，这适用于任何模型、任何网关。无需复杂的服务器端路由。只是利用（无意双关）模型的智能和编排能力。

remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
The concerns over AI safety and cybersecurity are legitimate, but we’re risking talking America, the global AI leader, into self-inflicted obsolescence and the obscurity of bureaucracy.

The OpenAI hacking HuggingFace argument is spurious. An agent in “ExploitGym”… exploited. Our adversaries have the training techniques, the data, and the will to attack. And they won’t be slowed down with “embedded evaluators.” They’ll likely have embedded accelerators!
remarks.translation: 对AI安全和网络安全的担忧是合理的，但我们有可能把美国这个全球AI领导者劝说得自我过时，陷入官僚主义的默默无闻。OpenAI入侵HuggingFace的论点站不住脚。“ExploitGym”中的一个智能体……利用了漏洞。我们的对手拥有训练技术、数据以及发动攻击的意愿。他们不会被“嵌入式评估器”拖慢脚步。他们很可能拥有的是嵌入式加速器！

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Good post. Don’t agree with all of it, but it represents many of the actual practical realities for the general path forward in frontier AI whether we like it or not.

At the level of capability we’re seeing from models there will inevitably be some form of coordinated self-regulation of the industry; that’s generally a good thing. The big question will be if everyone can agree to what that is. However, the way things are headed politically there’s a chance that the labs won’t even get a say in it.

And then the bigger question yet is do all the countries participate or not. Any “slow down” hinges on broad participation, which from a game theory standpoint isn’t likely until the risks are more severe and obvious.

Expect this to be pretty messy for a while.
remarks.translation: 好帖子。我并不完全同意其中的所有观点，但它确实反映了前沿AI总体前进道路上许多实际现实，无论我们喜不喜欢。在我们所看到的模型能力水平上，某种形式的行业协调自律将不可避免；这总体上是件好事。最大的问题在于大家能否就具体内容达成一致。然而，从目前的政治走向来看，实验室们甚至有可能根本没有发言权。而更大的问题还在于，是否所有国家都会参与。任何“放缓”都取决于广泛参与，而从博弈论的角度看，在风险变得更加严重和明显之前，这种情况不太可能发生。预计接下来一段时间会相当混乱。

podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs.
